newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends up at intra-day high vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends up at intra-day high vs dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at an intra-day high of 8.2960 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2975 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
The closing rate was the highest since June 8, 1995, when the yuan ended at 8.2959.
Traders said that most banks in the market sold their dollar reserves today due to expectations that China will post a large trade surplus this year.

The yuan opened up at an intra-day high of 8.2960 and fell to move around the 8.2965 level for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2974 at mid-session before rising again to the day's highest level.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2965, traders said.
One trader said that the market expected more dollar inflow due to China's strong foreign trade position this year.

"The central government usually announces the previous month's foreign trade data in mid-month," he said. "Investors believe this month's announcement will be good news for foreign trade, which will benefit the yuan's uptrend."
A second trader said that he believed the yuan would meet resistance at the 8.2950 level in the short term.
Traders expect the yuan to move below 8.2950 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed slightly down at 7.4505 from 7.4450 against 100 Japanese yen and up at an intra-day high of 1.0725 from 1.0740 against the Hong Kong dollar.
